purpose: Robustness of the rule-switch crossover to lazy revision (each interior trader adopts its rule output with probability alpha per step) and to band-rule technical traders placed in the interior at fraction rho
model_changes: revision_probability = alpha and interior_technical_fraction = rho in simulate(); alpha = 1 and rho = 0 reproduce the archived manuscript runs bit for bit

experiments.lazy: L = 64, rho = 0, alpha in {1, 0.95, 0.9, 0.75, 0.5}, held h = 100 and active h = 1, 100
experiments.interior: L = 64, alpha = 1, rho in {63 cells (edge count), 0.025, 0.05, 0.10}, held h = 100 and active h = 1, 100; rho = 0 is the lazy alpha = 1 condition
experiments.size: L = 32 and 128: alpha = 0.9 held h = 100; rho = 0.05 held and active h = 100; L = 64 counterparts are in the lazy and interior experiments

fraction_centers: Pilot crossovers (20 starting markets, seeds 1-20); see conditions in Prepare.py
seeds: 1-50, the starting markets of the manuscript campaigns
pairing: One no-switch control per condition and starting market, at the largest fraction with the minor rule dormant; exact common-history assertions for each switched run
majority: Interior Sell fraction, excluding interior technical traders, reaches 0.5 after the switch
estimands: Majority probability by fraction with Wilson 95% intervals; f25, f50, f75 by linear interpolation at the first upward crossing; paired differences in f50 between conditions sharing starting markets
uncertainty: 2,000 bootstrap resamples of whole starting markets, shared across conditions
resolution_check: Flag any condition with fewer than five fractions strictly between 0.05 and 0.95
validation: alpha = 1, rho = 0, L = 64 runs at fractions also run in the manuscript campaigns must reproduce the archived final-grid hashes in the ledger
